verdict.rationale: The pack never documents a native suppression-list API that lets you read, add or remove suppressed addresses. SES does publish bounce and complaint events through SNS or event destinations, and it monitors bounce and complaint rates. An app could use those events to build and maintain its own suppression list, so it never re-emails a hard bounce. Unsubscribe handling appears only as something you build yourself on top of SES. Missing for 10: a documented first-party suppression-list API (list, get, put, delete suppressed destinations), built-in unsubscribe suppression, automatic hard-bounce suppression behavior, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
